grammarFocus: 否定、比较、数量范围和时态；限定词的含义。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.
sourcePolicy: Project-original scenario; simulated figures and people; no copied official test, textbook, GitHub PDF or third-party audio.
title: Unequal Access: A School Board Meeting on Enrollment Zones
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数。请先听/读英文材料，再完成10道题（判断题、填空题、单选题、匹配题）。所有题目和选项均为英文；解释为中文。听力部分包含自然对话与更正，请留意说话人如何修正信息。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道新句子的语法题。最后完成口语与写作迁移任务。建议先不看答案，独立完成后再核对解释与证据。
transcript:
Maya Chen: Good evening, everyone. I'm Maya Chen, chair of the Westbrook District school board. Tonight we discuss the new enrollment zones for Northside High and Riverbend High. Before we start, I want to say clearly: no final vote happens tonight. We are only collecting comments.

Daniel Ortiz: Thank you, Chair Chen. I'm Daniel Ortiz, parent of a seventh-grader. My main worry is busing. If Northside takes students from the east side, how long will the ride be? Forty minutes? Fifty?

Maya Chen: The transport office estimates thirty-five to forty-five minutes for the farthest streets. Not fifty. I checked that number this morning.

Daniel Ortiz: All right, thirty-five to forty-five. That is still long for a twelve-year-old.

Priya Nair: I'm Priya Nair, and I teach science at Riverbend. I want to correct something I heard in the hallway. People say Riverbend has fewer lab spaces than Northside. That is not true. Riverbend has four labs; Northside has three. The real problem is not the number of labs. It is that our labs are older.

Maya Chen: Thank you for the correction. So the issue is age, not quantity.

Priya Nair: Exactly. And one more point: not every Riverbend student lives far away. About sixty percent walk or cycle. Only a minority depend on buses.

Tom Becker: I'm Tom Becker, from the parent council. I have a question about capacity. Northside can hold nine hundred students. Riverbend can hold seven hundred and fifty. Right now Northside has eight hundred and ten, and Riverbend has seven hundred and ninety. So Riverbend is already over its limit, and Northside is not full.

Maya Chen: That matches our data. Riverbend is forty students over capacity. Northside has ninety empty seats.

Tom Becker: Then why move more students to Riverbend? That makes no sense to me.

Maya Chen: The proposal does not move students to Riverbend. It moves a small group from the crowded east side to Northside. I think you have the direction reversed.

Tom Becker: Oh — I did have it reversed. Sorry. So the east-side group goes to Northside.

Maya Chen: Yes. About one hundred and twenty students would move. Not two hundred. One hundred and twenty.

Daniel Ortiz: Can I ask about timing? My daughter starts high school next year. Will the change apply to her?

Maya Chen: The new zones would begin in September of next year. Students already in grade ten or eleven would not be forced to move. Only incoming grade nine students and new arrivals would follow the new map.

Priya Nair: That is an important detail. So current older students stay.

Maya Chen: Correct. They stay if they choose to stay. Nobody is removed from a school they already attend.

Tom Becker: What about the budget? I read that the change saves money. Is that right?

Maya Chen: Partly. The district expects to save on bus fuel, but it will spend more on extra classrooms at Northside. The savings are smaller than the new costs. So the plan is not mainly about money.

Daniel Ortiz: Then what is it mainly about?

Maya Chen: Fair access. East-side students currently travel farther to reach a school with fewer science labs. Northside has more lab space and shorter trips for those families. The aim is to reduce that inequality.

Priya Nair: I support the aim, but I want a promise. If Northside gets more students, it needs more teachers, not just more rooms.

Maya Chen: That is a fair request. I will add it to the minutes: teacher numbers must grow with student numbers.

Tom Becker: One last thing. When is the next public meeting?

Maya Chen: The next meeting is on the fourteenth of March, at seven in the evening, in the Northside library. Not the Riverbend library — Northside. Please check the district website before you come, because the room may change.

Daniel Ortiz: Thank you. That was clearer than the last meeting.

Maya Chen: Thank you all. Remember: comments tonight, no vote tonight.

grammar.title: 否定、比较、数量范围与限定词
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 否定词 not 的位置与含义（not every = 并非每一个；not mainly = 主要不是）。2) 比较结构：fewer ... than, more ... than, smaller than, over capacity。3) 数量范围：about, only, at least, between ... and ...。4) 限定词：every, each, all, some, most, a minority of, none of。注意限定词决定名词范围：every student 是全部单个看；most students 是大多数；a minority 是少数。时态上，现在完成（has grown）表示已发生并影响现在；一般将来（will begin）表示计划。
grammar.example: Only a minority depend on buses.

options: Not every student lives far from school.
Not every students live far from school.
Every students do not live far from school.
Not all student lives far from school.
answers: Not every student lives far from school.
questions.explanation: not every + 单数名词 + 单数动词，表示“并非每一个”。
questions.evidence: Only a minority depend on buses.

options: Riverbend has fewer labs than Northside.
Riverbend has less labs than Northside.
Riverbend has few labs than Northside.
Riverbend has fewer labs that Northside.
answers: Riverbend has fewer labs than Northside.
questions.explanation: 可数名词复数用 fewer ... than；less 用于不可数。
questions.evidence: Riverbend has four labs; Northside has three.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about quantity.
options: About one hundred and twenty students would move.
About one hundred and twenty student would move.
About one hundred and twenty students will moved.
About one hundred and twenty students would moves.
answers: About one hundred and twenty students would move.
questions.explanation: about + 数量 + 复数名词；would + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: About one hundred and twenty students would move.

options: Most students walk or cycle.
Most student walk or cycle.
Most of students walks or cycle.
The most students walk or cycle.
questions.explanation: most + 复数名词，表示大多数；不用 the most students。
questions.evidence: About sixty percent walk or cycle.

options: The plan is not mainly about money.
The plan is not main about money.
The plan does not mainly money.
The plan not is mainly about money.
answers: The plan is not mainly about money.
questions.explanation: be 动词否定：is not + 副词 mainly + about。
questions.evidence: So the plan is not mainly about money.

options: The new zones will begin next September.
The new zones will begins next September.
The new zones begin will next September.
The new zones began will next September.
answers: The new zones will begin next September.
questions.explanation: 一般将来 will + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: The new zones would begin in September of next year.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'none of' with a singular verb in formal written English.
options: None of the students is forced to move.
None of the students are forced to move.
None of student is forced to move.
None students is forced to move.
answers: None of the students is forced to move.
questions.explanation: none of + 复数名词，正式书面语可用单数动词 is；本题明确要求正式书面语中的单数动词，因此只有该选项符合。
questions.evidence: Nobody is removed from a school they already attend.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence with 'at least'.
options: Northside needs at least five new teachers.
Northside needs at least five new teacher.
Northside need at least five new teachers.
Northside needs at less five new teachers.
answers: Northside needs at least five new teachers.
questions.explanation: at least + 数量 + 复数名词；主语 Northside 单数用 needs。
questions.evidence: teacher numbers must grow with student numbers.
